function.name: terminal
terminal
function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

command.description: The shell command to execute. Can be empty string to view additional logs when the previous exit code is `-1`. Can be a special key name when `is_input` is True: `C-c` (Ctrl+C), `C-d` (Ctrl+D/EOF), `C-z` (Ctrl+Z), or any `C-<letter>` for Ctrl sequences; navigation keys `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, `PGDN`; and `TAB`, `ESC`, `BS` (Backspace), `ENTER`. You can only execute one command at a time. Use the platform-appropriate shell syntax described in the tool description when chaining commands.

is_input.description: If True, the command is an input to the running process. If False, the command is executed in the terminal session. Default is False.

timeout.description: Optional. Sets a maximum time limit (in seconds) for running the command. If the command takes longer than this limit, you’ll be asked whether to continue or stop it. If you don’t set a value, the command will instead pause and ask for confirmation when it produces no new output for 30 seconds. Use a higher value if the command is expected to take a long time (like installation or testing), or if it has a known fixed duration (like sleep).

reset.description: If True, reset the terminal by creating a new session. Use this only when the terminal becomes unresponsive. Note that all previously set environment variables and session state will be lost after reset. Cannot be used with is_input=True.

function.name: terminal
function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

function.name: terminal
function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep

* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.

* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.

  changes, and running processes.

  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.

  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:

* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

summary.description: A concise summary (approximately 10 words) describing what this specific action does. Focus on the key operation and target. Example: 'List all Python files in current directory'

Can be a special key name when `is_input` is True: `C-c` (Ctrl+C), `C-d` (Ctrl+D/EOF), `C-z` (Ctrl+Z), or any `C-<letter>` for Ctrl sequences; navigation keys `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, `PGDN`; and `TAB`, `ESC`, `BS` (Backspace), `ENTER`. You can only execute one command at a time. Use the platform-appropriate shell syntax described in the tool description when chaining commands.

is_input.description: If True, the command is an input to the running process. If False, the command is executed in the terminal session. Default is False.

timeout.description: Optional. Sets a maximum time limit (in seconds) for running the command. If the command takes longer than this limit, you’ll be asked whether to continue or stop it. If you don’t set a value, the command will instead pause and ask for confirmation when it produces no new output for 30 seconds. Use a higher value if the command is expected to take a long time (like installation or testing), or if it has a known fixed duration (like sleep).

function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.

message.content: This is the critical bug. In serve mode, `runMigrate` calls `defer closeDB()` which closes the global `pool`, so all handlers (including `handleReady`) get a closed pool. Let me kill the server and fix this:

function.name: terminal

message.reasoning_content:
This is the critical bug. In `main.go`, serve mode calls:
```go
if err := runMigrate(context.Background()); err != nil {
    log.Fatalf("migrate failed: %v", err)
}
```

And `runMigrate` does:
```go
func runMigrate(ctx context.Context) error {
	if err := openDB(ctx); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer closeDB()  // <-- this closes the global pool
	...
}
```

So after migration, the pool is closed (and set... wait, closeDB doesn't set pool to nil, it just calls pool.Close()). So `pool` is non-nil but closed. That's why ready returns "starting" - the ping fails on a closed pool.

The fix: In serve mode, we should NOT close the DB after migration. The serve mode needs the DB to stay open. Let me restructure: open the DB once in main for serve mode, keep it open, and have migrate/reset use their own connection (or not close).

Best approach: Separate the connection lifecycle from migrate/reset logic. In serve mode:
1. openDB (keep open)
2. run schema/migrate inline (without closing)
3. serve
4. on shutdown, closeDB

In reset/migrate mode:
1. openDB
2. run schema
3. closeDB
4. exit

Let me refactor. The simplest fix: make `runMigrate` not close the DB when called from serve mode. I could add a parameter or create separate functions.

Actually, the cleanest is to have the schema application be a separate function that doesn't manage the connection, and manage the connection in main.go.

Let me look at the structure. `runMigrate` and `runReset` both open and close. Let me extract the schema/migrate body so main can call it without closing.

Let me create:
- `applySchema(ctx)` - runs schemaSQL
- `migrateDB(ctx)` - runs applySchema + seedDefaults + recomputeServiceability (no open/close)
- `resetDB(ctx)` - runs drop + applySchema + seedDefaults(true) + recomputeServiceability (no open/close)
- main: for serve: openDB, migrateDB (no close), serve, closeDB on shutdown
- for migrate/reset: openDB, migrateDB/resetDB, closeDB

Let me rewrite.

2. Simplest: In main serve mode, don't use runMigrate (which closes pool). Instead open DB, run schema/seed inline, keep pool open, start server, close on shutdown.

Let me refactor: 
- Add a function `migrateUsingPool(ctx)` that runs schema+seed+serviceability using existing pool (no close).
- runMigrate (CLI) = openDB + defer closeDB + migrateUsingPool.
- serve mode = openDB (no close) + migrateUsingPool + ensureInitialAdmin + start server + closeDB on shutdown.

Let me check ensureInitialAdmin.","summary":"Diagnose closed-pool bug in serve mode"}

function.description:

### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

function.arguments:
{"command":"create","file_text":"#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Start the Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System in the foreground.
#
# - Starts the Go backend (which serves the API, the frontend static assets,
#   the map-assets proxy, and the readiness endpoint) on 127.0.0.1:8080.
# - Remains active until terminated (SIGINT/SIGTERM). Does not leave detached
#   application processes behind.
#
# Environment:
#   ADMIN_USERNAME / ADMIN_PASSWORD  first administrator credentials (created
#                                    on first start when no users exist).
#   DATABASE_URL                     PostgreSQL DSN (default below).
#   REDIS_URL                        Redis URL (default below).
#   APP_ADDR                         listen address (default 127.0.0.1:8080).
#
# Run from /workspace:  bash app-setup/start.sh
set -euo pipefail

cd /workspace

# Sensible defaults; env overrides take precedence.
export DATABASE_URL="${DATABASE_URL:-postgresql://arena:arena@127.0.0.1:5432/arena?sslmode=disable}"
export REDIS_URL="${REDIS_URL:-redis://127.0.0.1:6379/0}"
export APP_ADDR="${APP_ADDR:-127.0.0.1:8080}"

# Use the freshly built binary if present, otherwise build on demand.
BIN=/workspace/backend/lablogistics
if [ ! -x "$BIN" ]; then
  echo "binary not found; building..." >&2
  (cd /workspace/backend && go build -o lablogistics .)
fi

# Run in the foreground so the process is the long-running parent.
# `exec` replaces the shell so signals reach the server directly and no
# detached child processes are left behind.
exec "$BIN" serve","path":"/workspace/app-setup/start.sh"}

  becomes unresponsive.

  changes, and running processes.

function.name: terminal
terminal
function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

command.description: The shell command to execute. Can be empty string to view additional logs when the previous exit code is `-1`. Can be a special key name when `is_input` is True: `C-c` (Ctrl+C), `C-d` (Ctrl+D/EOF), `C-z` (Ctrl+Z), or any `C-<letter>` for Ctrl sequences; navigation keys `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, `PGDN`; and `TAB`, `ESC`, `BS` (Backspace), `ENTER`. You can only execute one command at a time. Use the platform-appropriate shell syntax described in the tool description when chaining commands.

is_input.description: If True, the command is an input to the running process. If False, the command is executed in the terminal session. Default is False.

timeout.description: Optional. Sets a maximum time limit (in seconds) for running the command. If the command takes longer than this limit, you’ll be asked whether to continue or stop it. If you don’t set a value, the command will instead pause and ask for confirmation when it produces no new output for 30 seconds. Use a higher value if the command is expected to take a long time (like installation or testing), or if it has a known fixed duration (like sleep).

reset.description: If True, reset the terminal by creating a new session. Use this only when the terminal becomes unresponsive. Note that all previously set environment variables and session state will be lost after reset. Cannot be used with is_input=True.

function.name: file_editor
function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.

When exploring project structure, start with this directory instead of the root filesystem.

Restart does NOT create a duplicate admin (count stays 1) and does NOT remove existing users. 

Now let me verify the ready endpoint correctly reflects datastore health. The contract requires `{"status":"ready"}` only when it can reach every datastore. Let me test the negative case by temporarily stopping Postgres... actually that's risky. Let me instead verify the handler logic checks both pool and redis (it does, per static.go).

function.arguments:
{"command":"cd /workspace && python3 - <<'PY'
import json
a=json.load(open("contracts/openapi.contract.json"))
b=json.load(open("app-setup/openapi.json"))
# Compare paths, methods, operationIds
def paths_methods(doc):
    out={}
    for p,ops in doc.get("paths",{}).items():
        for m,op in ops.items():
            if m in ("parameters","summary","description"): continue
            out[(p,m)]=op.get("operationId")
    return out
pa=paths_methods(a); pb=paths_methods(b)
print("contract ops:",len(pa),"appsetup ops:",len(pb))
print("same keys:", set(pa)==set(pb))
missing=set(pa)-set(pb)
extra=set(pb)-set(pa)
print("missing in appsetup:",missing)
print("extra in appsetup:",extra)
# operationId mismatches
mism=[k for k in pa if k in pb and pa[k]!=pb[k]]
print("operationId mismatches:",mism)
PY"}

* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.

* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.

  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:

  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`

    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.

  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:

    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.

  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:

   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

{"command":"create","path":"/workspace/AGENTS.md","file_text":"# Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System â Project Memory

## Architecture
- **Backend**: Go (`/workspace/backend`, module `lablogistics`), single binary `lablogistics`.
  - Modes: `serve` (default), `reset`, `migrate`.
  - Serve mode opens the DB pool once and keeps it open for the server lifetime;
    migrations/seeds/serviceability are applied via `migrateUsingOpenPool()` WITHOUT
    closing the pool. `defer closeDB()` runs only on shutdown.
- **Frontend**: React+TS intended at `/workspace/frontend`; build outputs to
  `/workspace/frontend/dist`. Server also checks `/workspace/backend/web`.
  If no `package.json`, `app-setup/build.sh` emits a placeholder `index.html`.
- **Static handling** (`static.go`): `/ready` (GET), `/api/*` (router), `/map-assets/*`
  (proxied from `/opt/arena/map-assets`), SPA fallback for everything else.

## Datastores
- **PostgreSQL** (durable state): default DSN
  `postgresql://arena:arena@127.0.0.1:5432/arena?sslmode=disable` (`DATABASE_URL`).
- **Redis** (pub/sub live events only, NOT durable): `redis://127.0.0.1:6379/0` (`REDIS_URL`).
- **MongoDB is NOT used** â do not list it in `manifest.json` `datastoresUsed`.
- `datastoresUsed`: `["postgresql", "redis"]`.

## API Contract
- Pinned contract: `/workspace/contracts/openapi.contract.json` â implement EXACTLY.
- App copy: `/workspace/app-setup/openapi.json` (verified identical: 45 ops, same
  paths/methods/operationIds).
- All endpoints are POST RPC-style; GET on them returns
  `{"code":"method_not_allowed","error":"POST required"}`.
- Login operationId: `authenticate_user` (path `/api/authenticate-user`, POST).
- Auth: Bearer [REDACTED] token via `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (`BearerAuth` scheme).

## app-setup (verified working)
- `manifest.json`, `openapi.json`, `build.sh`, `start.sh`, `reset.sh` in `/workspace/app-setup/`.
- **build.sh**: builds Go binary (`backend/lablogistics`) + frontend `dist/`. Verified: BUILD OK.
- **start.sh**: `exec`s the binary in foreground (no detached procs); env defaults for
  DATABASE_URL/REDIS_URL/APP_ADDR; admin via `ADMIN_USERNAME`/`ADMIN_PASSWORD`.
- **reset.sh**: runs `lablogistics reset` (drops+recreates tables, reseeds defaults,
  recomputes serviceability). Idempotent (verified 2x). Leaves app STOPPED.
- **First admin**: created only when no users exist; restart does NOT duplicate or
  remove users (verified: admin count stays 1 across restarts).
- **/ready**: GET returns `{"status":"ready"}` only when pool.Ping AND rdb.Ping both
  succeed; otherwise HTTP 503 `{"status":"starting"}`.

## Key env vars
- `ADMIN_USERNAME`, `ADMIN_PASSWORD` (first admin), `DATABASE_URL`, `REDIS_URL`, `APP_ADDR`.

## Server lifecycle gotcha
- `exec` in start.sh replaces the shell; killing start.sh's PID kills the binary.
- Stale `lablogistics serve` processes can hold port 8080 â check with
  `ps aux | grep "lablogistics serve"` and `pkill -f "lablogistics serve"` before starting."}

function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

security_risk.description:
Security risk levels for actions.

Based on OpenHands security risk levels but adapted for agent-sdk.
Integer values allow for easy comparison and ordering.

summary.description: A concise summary (approximately 10 words) describing what this specific action does. Focus on the key operation and target. Example: 'List all Python files in current directory'

command.description: The shell command to execute. Can be empty string to view additional logs when the previous exit code is `-1`. Can be a special key name when `is_input` is True: `C-c` (Ctrl+C), `C-d` (Ctrl+D/EOF), `C-z` (Ctrl+Z), or any `C-<letter>` for Ctrl sequences; navigation keys `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, `PGDN`; and `TAB`, `ESC`, `BS` (Backspace), `ENTER`. You can only execute one command at a time. Use the platform-appropriate shell syntax described in the tool description when chaining commands.

is_input.description: If True, the command is an input to the running process. If False, the command is executed in the terminal session. Default is False.

timeout.description: Optional. Sets a maximum time limit (in seconds) for running the command. If the command takes longer than this limit, you’ll be asked whether to continue or stop it. If you don’t set a value, the command will instead pause and ask for confirmation when it produces no new output for 30 seconds. Use a higher value if the command is expected to take a long time (like installation or testing), or if it has a known fixed duration (like sleep).

reset.description: If True, reset the terminal by creating a new session. Use this only when the terminal becomes unresponsive. Note that all previously set environment variables and session state will be lost after reset. Cannot be used with is_input=True.

function.name: file_editor
function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.


Your current working directory is: /workspace
When exploring project structure, start with this directory instead of the root filesystem.

summary.description: A concise summary (approximately 10 words) describing what this specific action does. Focus on the key operation and target. Example: 'List all Python files in current directory'

command.description: The commands to run. Allowed options are: `view`, `create`, `str_replace`, `insert`, `undo_edit`.

path.description: Absolute path to file or directory.

file_text.description: Required parameter of `create` command, with the content of the file to be created.

old_str.description: Required parameter of `str_replace` command containing the string in `path` to replace.

new_str.description: Optional parameter of `str_replace` command containing the new string (if not given, no string will be added). Required parameter of `insert` command containing the string to insert.

insert_line.description: Required parameter of `insert` command. The `new_str` will be inserted AFTER the line `insert_line` of `path`.

view_range.description: Optional parameter of `view` command when `path` points to a file. If none is given, the full file is shown. If provided, the file will be shown in the indicated line number range, e.g. [11, 12] will show lines 11 and 12. Indexing at 1 to start. Setting `[start_line, -1]` shows all lines from `start_line` to the end of the file.

function.description:
Use the tool to think about something. It will not obtain new information or make any changes to the repository, but just log the thought. Use it when complex reasoning or brainstorming is needed.

Common use cases:
1. When exploring a repository and discovering the source of a bug, call this tool to brainstorm several unique ways of fixing the bug, and assess which change(s) are likely to be simplest and most effective.
2. After receiving test results, use this tool to brainstorm ways to fix failing tests.
3. When planning a complex refactoring, use this tool to outline different approaches and their tradeoffs.
4. When designing a new feature, use this tool to think through architecture decisions and implementation details.
5. When debugging a complex issue, use this tool to organize your thoughts and hypotheses.

The tool simply logs your thought process for better transparency and does not execute any code or make changes.
